name: Blue-capped Redstart
rangeDescription: Montane juniper and pine forest of southern asia
description: An odd small redstart of open dry forests. Male doesn’t look like any other redstarts; somewhat resembles magpie-robins, which do not share its range.

name: Jerdon's Leafbird
rangeDescription: Peninsular india and sri lanka
description: Crisp emerald-green forest-dweller. Male has a dark blue throat patch outlined by a thick black border.

name: San Andres Vireo
rangeDescription: Mangroves of isla san andrés (to far northwest of colombia, off eastern nicaragua)
description: A hyperactive inhabitant of brush and mangroves; largely pursues insects near the ground and at moderate heights. This species has a green back that contrasts with a gray crown, white wingbars, and a yellow stripe from the upper bill to the eye.

name: Fatu Hiva Monarch
rangeDescription: Fatuhiva (southern marquesas islands)
description: A distinctive large glossy-black flycatcher with a pale bluish-ivory bill. Bushy feathers give an eyebrowed appearance.

name: Green-backed Firecrown
rangeDescription: Central chile and argentina to tierra del fuego; juan fernández islands (far west of central chile)
description: The only hummingbird in most of southernmost South America. Fairly common to common in woodlands, forests, gardens, matorral, and flowering hedges and bushes in farmland of lowlands and foothills.

name: Himalayan Shortwing
rangeDescription: Eastern himalayas to northern myanmar and western china; winters to northern indochina
description: Tiny, stumpy bird of dense undergrowth. Male is dark slate-blue with broad white eyebrows that give him the appearance of a furious little old man.

name: White-bearded Antshrike
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southeastern minas gerais) to far northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Unmistakable medium-sized antshrike, with a long tail and a short bill. Inhabits the understory of dense humid forest and second growth with bamboo.

name: Newton's Sunbird
rangeDescription: São tomé island (gulf of guinea)
description: A small sunbird with dark olive upperparts. Male has an iridescent green-purple throat and upper breast; female has a dull scaly olive throat and yellowish underparts.

name: Pacific Heron
rangeDescription: Wetlands of australia including tasmania
description: Large dark gray heron with white head and neck. In flight shows white

name: White-breasted Guineafowl
rangeDescription: Upper guinea forest of southeastern sierra leone to ivory coast and western ghana
description: Small, long-tailed, mostly black guineafowl with a white ruff around the neck and a bare red head. Found on the ground in lowland rainforest.

name: Caucasian Grouse
rangeDescription: Caucasus mountains, from far southwestern russia eastward to northeastern azerbaijan and southward to northeastern turkey, armenia, and far northwestern iran
description: Large gamebird endemic to the mountains of the Caucasus region. Male is jet-black with a tiny white patch on the shoulder, a tail that curves downwards at the tip, and flaming red “eyebrows.” White underwing patches are displayed during jumping lekking display.

name: Sagebrush Sparrow
rangeDescription: Sagebrush and saltbush of great basin
description: Pale, subtly-patterned sparrow. Sandy-brown overall with gray head and whitish breast with dark central spotting.

name: Turquoise Cotinga
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southwestern costa rica to western panama (western chiriquí)
description: Unmistakable in range: male is stunning electric-blue with purple patch on throat and belly. Female completely different; pale grayish with heavy spotting below and scaling on back.

name: Hose's Broadbill
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed submontane forest of northern and central borneo
description: Uncommon and elusive green broadbill. Both sexes distinguished from other Bornean green broadbills by blue wash on belly; it is bright ultramarine in males and paler blue in females.

name: Mangrove Finch
rangeDescription: Mangroves on northwest coast of isabela (galapagos); restricted to very small area, formerly also on eastern coast of isabela, and on fernandina
description: A critically endangered Galápagos finch and one of the world’s rarest birds. Currently known only from mangroves at a few sites (with restricted access) on Isabela.

name: Blue-capped Redstart
rangeDescription: Montane juniper and pine forest of southern asia
description: An odd small redstart of open dry forests. Male doesn’t look like any other redstarts; somewhat resembles magpie-robins, which do not share its range.

name: Broad-billed Tody
rangeDescription: Arid scrub and woodland of hispaniola including gonâve island
description: A small, gemlike species of woodlands including coffee plantations and mangroves. The rather large head, long bill, and short tail create a profile shared only by the Narrow-billed Tody within its range.

name: Rachel's Malimbe
rangeDescription: Lowland forest of southeastern nigeria to southern cameroon and gabon
description: A beautiful malimbe locally distributed in Central Africa and restricted to lowland primary forest and its edges, where it is often found high above the ground in small groups or with mixed-species flocks, sometimes with other species of malimbe. Both males and females are wholly black with yellow vents and orange chests that fade to yellow at the edges.

name: Buff-faced Scrubwren
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of central and eastern new guinea
description: A very small, drab bird of montane forest understory. Pale brown underparts, dark brown upperparts, Gray from the crown to upper back widening to a half-collar.

name: Serra do Mar Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal mountains of southeastern brazil (espírito santo to northern rio grande do sul)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a long slender tail. Differs from other tyrannulets in being mostly bright olive-green above and gray below with darkish ear patches, prominent white eyerings, and pinkish (not dark) legs.
